definitions.explanation: A speech sound produced by partially or fully obstructing airflow, as opposed to a vowel. In Japanese linguistics, consonants combine with vowels to form syllables in the kana system.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{子音|しいん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧。
examples.english: Japanese has fewer consonants than English.

examples.japanese: {子音|しいん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{母音|ぼいん}→母音：13205_boin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{組|く}み{合|あ}わせ→組み合わせ：13794_kumiawase⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{音節|おんせつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: Syllables are formed by combining consonants and vowels.

notes:
{子音|しいん} is the opposite of ⟦{母音|ぼいん}→母音：13205_boin⟧ (vowel).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {子音|しいん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{母音|ぼいん}→母音：13205_boin⟧ — consonants and vowels
- {有声|ゆうせい}{子音|しいん} — voiced consonant
- {無声|むせい}{子音|しいん} — voiceless consonant
- {子音|しいん}⟦{連続|れんぞく}→連続：03783_renzoku⟧ — consonant cluster

In Japanese phonology, most syllables consist of one {子音|しいん} followed by one ⟦{母音|ぼいん}→母音：13205_boin⟧ (CV structure), with the notable exception of ん (the moraic nasal).
